newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SHARE OF SUPERSPORT TITLE CLAIMED BY NATAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SHARE OF SUPERSPORT TITLE CLAIMED BY NATAL.

text.p: Natal took at least a share of the Supersport Series title without taking a point on the first day of their match against Western Province at Newlands on Friday.

By denying Western Province a fourth batting bonus point they made it mathematically impossible to be overhauled, although in turn, Province kept alive their faint hopes of at least sharing the title by preventing Natal taking any bowling bonus points.
Natal -- which went into the match with a 17-point lead over Western Province -- now need just one batting bonus point to claim the title outright.
After being put in on a greenish, well-grassed wicket, Western Province batted serenely throughout the day to close on 269 for two.
Desmond Haynes, in what may be his final first-class match, scored 83, and with Jacques Kallis (90 not out) and Herschelle Gibbs (47 not out) in unusally circumspect mood, Natal laboured in vain.
Province lost test opener Gary Kirsten for 20 after an hour and a half's play before a measured 112-run partnership in 40 overs between Haynes and Kallis set the tone for the day.
Haynes was eventually winkled out by off-spinner Pat Symcox after a four innings which included six fours and one six.

Kallis was becalmed on six for an hour and took 95 minutes to reach double figures but gathered pace thereafter and had batted just over five hours with seven fours and one six to be ten short of three figures at the close.
Province need to bowl out Natal for less than 150 and win the match to share the title.
